answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a verifiable delay function on a CPU thread. Each epoch, a beacon emits a randomness pulse that nodes feed into sequential squarings in a class group, posting a short proof before a tight deadline. Because the steps resist parallelization, attackers cannot forge proofs without sequential work, forcing dedicated cores and power per identity. However, custom ASICs evaluate faster and undercut commodity CPUs.
